clue.text: Mum's hiding garb of yesteryear (flowery things)

indicators.note: the word for mum with its possessive wraps round the clothing pieces, so it is hiding them

parts.note: mum is MA, and the possessive adds S
rig is an informal word for clothing or garb
something of yesteryear is old

explanation.surface: Mother is concealing the old-fashioned clothes she once wore, with flowers mentioned in passing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' tempts as the chrysanthemum flower, but it is mother; 'hiding' means her possessive name wraps round the old clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Marigolds are bright garden flowers, here jokingly called flowery things.

clue.text: Lady married Adam's son

parts.note: Abel was a son of Adam and Eve in Genesis

explanation.surface: A woman wed one of the sons of the first man.
explanation.definitionFit: Mabel is a woman's name, so an example of a lady.

clue.text: Artist's item of furniture that may have price put on it

definitions.text: that may have price put on it

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, stands for an artist; the 's is a link
a table is an item of furniture

explanation.surface: A painter owns a piece of furniture that could be valued.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratable means able to be rated or valued, so a price can be put on it.

clue.text: Concerned with new criminal in fine territory for outlaws

indicators.note: the regarding word and scrambled letters sit inside the word for fine

parts.note: good means fine
RE means concerning or with regard to

indicators.note: criminal means bent or wrong, so the letters of new are jumbled

explanation.surface: A new lawbreaker is worried about life in fine bandit country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' scrambles the word new to give ENW; 'in' places it, with the regarding word, inside fine.
explanation.definitionFit: The greenwood is the forest where legendary outlaws such as Robin Hood lived.

clue.text: Sat for less than half this time

definitions.text: Sat for less than half this time

parts.words: Sat for less than half this time
parts.note: Sat is short for Saturday, which is under half of an extended break running from Friday to Monday

explanation.definitionFit: A long weekend adds a Friday or Monday off, so Saturday is under half of it.

clue.text: Popular holiday destination not favoured in spring

indicators.note: not means the favoured word is left out

parts.note: Spain is a hugely popular holiday country
in means fashionable or favoured

explanation.surface: A well-loved resort country has fallen out of favour this spring.
explanation.definitionFit: A spa is a mineral spring, or a town built around one.

clue.text: Money more than before? Review the evidence

parts.note: a sum is an amount of money
prices that are up are higher than they were before

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether there is more cash now, then turns to a judge's closing summary.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge's summing-up reviews the evidence for the jury; to sum up is to go over it in brief.

clue.text: Revolutionary city founder in old civilisation

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning right round, so the name reads backwards

parts.note: Remus, with his twin Romulus, was a legendary founder of Rome

explanation.surface: A rebel founded a city in an ancient civilisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumer was an ancient civilisation in southern Mesopotamia.

clue.text: Physicist has stuff put up about electrical current

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: to stuff is to cram
on means about, as in a book on birds
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A scientist has material hoisted round an electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: Guglielmo Marconi was the physicist and engineer who pioneered radio transmission.

clue.text: Patterns that could be made by a map with grids

indicators.note: the answer could be made by rearranging these letters

explanation.surface: Designs might be produced with a gridded map.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the two parts of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A paradigm is a model or typical pattern.

clue.text: Bird nipped across river

indicators.note: the bitten word stretches across the river letter, holding it inside

parts.note: nipped means bitten

explanation.surface: A bird gives someone a nip on the far side of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The bittern is a wading bird of the heron family known for its booming call.

clue.text: Fan of a doctor outside Slough?

indicators.note: the doctor abbreviation sits outside the bog word, wrapping it

parts.note: a slough is a swamp or bog, as is a mire

explanation.surface: Someone who admires a physician stands outside the town of Slough.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is a town west of London, but here it is a muddy bog, MIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: An admirer is a fan, someone devoted to a person or thing.

clue.text: Choreographer left with a deficient group of musicians

indicators.note: deficient means lacking something, here the last letter of the musicians' word

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians

explanation.surface: A dance-maker has been left with a band that is short of players.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolf Laban was a famous dance theorist and choreographer who devised a dance notation.

clue.text: Port or simple drink to be given to duke

parts.note: plain water is the simplest drink
something for someone is given to them

explanation.surface: A host offers port or, more simply, water to a visiting duke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the wine, offered alongside water, but it is a harbour town: Waterford is a port in south-east Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterford is an Irish city and harbour town, so it is an example of a port.

clue.text: Clare's place first to have panel game

indicators.note: the town is first to have the panel, which goes before it

parts.note: a tablet is a flat slab or panel
Ennis is the county town of County Clare in Ireland

explanation.surface: A Clare venue has the panel game on first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clare' is the Irish county; ENNIS is its county town.
explanation.definitionFit: Table tennis is the indoor bat-and-ball game also called ping-pong.

clue.text: Buzzer used in meeting

definitions.meaning: a gathering for a shared activity, as in a sewing or spelling gathering

explanation.definitionFit: A bee buzzes, and a bee is also a social gathering for work or competition, as in spelling bee.

clue.text: Some 'idden stuff gone over by cleaner in executive apartment

indicators.note: the cleaning tool goes over the stash, which ends up inside it

parts.note: a broom is a cleaning tool
a hoard is some hidden stuff; dropping the H as the clue's 'idden does gives OARD

explanation.surface: A broom sweeps over some hidden stash in the company's top room.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'idden shows the H is dropped, so the hoard loses its H as well.
explanation.definitionFit: A boardroom is where a company's directors meet, an executive room.

clue.text: Officious in respect of course to be taken

parts.note: over can mean about or concerning, as in a row over money
a bearing is a compass direction, the course taken

explanation.surface: A busybody fusses about which route the group should take.
explanation.definitionFit: Overbearing means domineering and bossy, close in sense to officious meddling.

clue.text: Old instrument that's broken in a lab store

indicators.note: broken means smashed apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An antique device is smashed in a laboratory storeroom.
explanation.definitionFit: An astrolabe is an early astronomical instrument for measuring the altitude of stars.

clue.text: Summary of a game intended for broadcast

parts.note: bridge is a card game

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken out, so the word is given by its sound

parts.note: intended means meant

explanation.surface: A précis of a match that was meant to go out on air.
explanation.definitionFit: An abridgement is a shortened version of a text, a kind of summary.

clue.text: Splendid journalist gets wined and dined

parts.note: regal means kingly, splendid
ED, editor, stands for a journalist

explanation.surface: A grand newspaperman is treated to a lavish meal.
explanation.definitionFit: To regale is to entertain lavishly with food and drink.

clue.text: We'll leave sailing centre for foreign island

indicators.note: the letters for we will leave, that is go out of, the town

parts.note: Cowes on the Isle of Wight is Britain's best-known yachting centre
we will: the letters W and E are the ones that go

explanation.surface: Sailors announce they are quitting the yachting town for an island abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: COWES is a yachting town on the Isle of Wight, home of Cowes Week; take out W and E to leave COS.
explanation.definitionFit: Cos, also spelt Kos, is a Greek island, so foreign to a British solver.

clue.text: Sugary French book with a twist at the end

indicators.text: with a twist at the end
indicators.note: the final pair of letters is twisted round

parts.note: Candide is Voltaire's French satirical novel

explanation.surface: A sweet French novel has a surprise ending.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the last two letters of CANDIDE swap, DE becoming ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Candied fruit is preserved in sugar, so candied means sugary.

clue.text: Does it enable your setter to get along swimmingly?

definitions.text: Does it enable your setter to get along swimmingly?

parts.words: Does it enable your setter to get along swimmingly?
parts.note: the setter is not the crossword compiler but a breed of hound, and the question asks what stroke lets such an animal move through water

explanation.definitionFit: The simplest swimming stroke, paddling the limbs like a swimming hound, is named after the animal.

clue.text: Sailor and crew heading off across the ship

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: the first letter, the head, of the crew word is taken away

parts.note: a team is a crew

explanation.surface: A sailor and the crew set off across the deck.
explanation.definitionFit: Abeam means at right angles to the ship's length, across it.

clue.text: One who has acquired nine points legally?

definitions.text: One who has acquired nine points legally?

parts.words: One who has acquired nine points legally?
parts.note: plays on the saying that possession is nine points of the law: whoever holds a thing has most of the legal claim

explanation.definitionFit: A person who possesses something holds it, so has the nine points the proverb gives possession.

clue.text: I get you Romeo's predecessor

definitions.meaning: a radio word meaning message received and understood
the older radio phonetic alphabet's word for R, before the current one

explanation.definitionFit: Roger means understood on the radio, and was the old phonetic name for R.

clue.text: One may get bored in the petroleum business

definitions.text: One may get bored in the petroleum business

parts.words: One may get bored in the petroleum business
parts.note: bored here means drilled, not weary: a shaft drilled to extract crude

explanation.definitionFit: A well for crude oil is made by boring into the ground, the basic unit of oil extraction.

clue.text: Beat is weak, lacking energy

indicators.note: lacking means without, so the energy letter is removed

parts.note: a lame excuse is a weak one
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A rhythm is feeble and has no energy.
explanation.definitionFit: To lam is to beat or thrash someone.

clue.text: Getting close to grannie can be awkward

indicators.note: awkward means out of order or clumsy, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Getting near to an old granny can be an uncomfortable business.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearing means approaching, coming close to something.

clue.text: Two thousand lines entering that electronic device

indicators.note: the poem goes into the pair of thousands, which surround it

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so two are MM
an ode is a poem, lines of verse

explanation.surface: Thousands of lines of code are being typed into a piece of computer kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A modem is a device that converts digital signals for transmission over phone lines.

clue.text: Acknowledgement of James Bond's boss as a deceptive type

parts.note: M is the head of the secret service in the James Bond stories
to acknowledge the spy chief is to say that he is leader

explanation.surface: Admitting that 007's chief is a con artist.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as 'M is leader', a statement acknowledging Bond's boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A misleader is someone who leads others astray, a deceiver.
